SCIENTIFIC-DATA-ANALYSIS
Release v2.6 measured usage / v2.5 deep budget-deferral hardening / v2.4 budget-architecture hardening / v2.3 modular architecture / v2.2 evaluation-hardening / v2.1 compact-router / v2.0 integrated skill + ScientificWorkbench / v1.9 contract-freeze / v1.8 app-ready backend / v1.7 real-world / v1.6 stable baseline

Compatibility anchors for historical gates: Release v1.7 stable / v1.6 stable baseline.
Historical exact anchors: Release v2.4 budget-architecture hardening; v2.3/v2.4 modular-health route.

What this release means
- v2.6 is the measured-usage release: it adds a benchmark matrix, local observed-usage harness, routing cost findings, app-ready cost sanity checks, and a guide explaining what can and cannot be inferred from proxy measurements.
- v2.6 does not promise weekly usage-limit savings from one local proxy run; it records evidence and keeps optimization conservative.
- v2.5 is the deep budget-deferral hardening release: astro and maintainer child skills keep stable script entrypoints while dispatching heavy bodies from fixtures, and the historical v2.3 ownership matrix is archived behind a compact maintainer stub.
- v2.5 closes the remaining required plugin-eval budget fixes for scientific-data-astro and scientific-data-maintainer without changing registry, ScientificWorkbench, or scientific behavior.
- v2.4 is the budget-architecture hardening release: heavy historical regression bodies, matrices, old guide payloads, and maintainer-only material live canonically in scientific-data-maintainer; the mother keeps compatibility wrappers and pointer stubs.
- v2.3 is the modular architecture release: scientific-data-analysis remains the mother-router while staged child skills cover astro, documents, notebooks, and maintainer routes without breaking historical command paths.
- v2.2 keeps transient outputs and caches out of the active bundle and replaces bulky historical routing with compatibility stubs.
- v2.1 keeps SKILL.md as a compact router while generated public-surface details and long routing notes live in references.
- v2.0 validates the installed skill with ScientificWorkbench as the native macOS product surface.
- v1.9 freezes artifact types, app-facing errors, app hints, next actions, exposure modes, and v2.0 deferrals.
- v1.8 defines the app-ready backend: JSON envelopes, run bundles, app-readiness matrix, dry-run router, and app-like regressions.
- v1.7 documents real-world applicability for public capabilities across academic, professional, and personal use.
- v1.6 remains the completed 59-capability audit-and-hardening baseline.

What this release promises
- Stable public script paths and registry labels.
- Stable scientific behavior and non-destructive workflows.
- Reproducible v2.6 measured-usage scenarios and regressions that compare broad mother routing with direct child routes where intent is already scoped.
- A v2.3/v2.4/v2.5 modular-health route: mother router, staged child skills, compatibility wrappers, maintainer-owned historical gates, fixture-backed script bodies, and a lower active budget for plugin-eval without losing public routes.
- Controlled optional-backend behavior for STILTS/TOPCAT, APT, TEAREDUCE, IRAF/iSTARMOD/fxcor, iWork, Keynote, and GUI-adjacent paths.
- Clear release validation through v2.5, v2.4, v2.3, sync-public-surface, smoke, and plugin-eval gates.

What this release does not promise
- No new public capabilities.
- No ScientificWorkbench synchronization or app development in v2.6.
- No claim that local proxy token estimates are real Codex account usage.
- No full removal of all budget warnings; remaining deferred budget, Python complexity, and long-line findings are accepted backlog unless they become required fixes.
